methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a local Norfolk native directly build community capacity through peer networks, demonstrating grassroots knowledge distribution outside traditional institutional channels—a key marker of distributed, deep adoption.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates academic AI infrastructure in the capital region, creating a potential hub but raising questions about whether this knowledge radiates beyond Richmond or deepens the metro capability advantage.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Analysis explicitly identifies AI data centers as widening Virginia's urban-rural divide, signaling that infrastructure concentration in NoVA actively creates distributional inequality rather than enabling statewide capability growth.

signals.title: University of Mary Washington Adds Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - Northern Virginia Magazine
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's first AI business master's degree at UMW creates deep technical-business capability but its centralized academic delivery model concentrates expertise rather than distributing fluency across workforce segments or regions.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard's deployment of 'Amelia' AI assistant represents platform-delivered shallow adoption—workers gain AI access without building underlying technical capability, fitting the shallow-but-distributed pattern if scaled beyond one facility.
